## Reflection

The call was driven by saturated, ultra-potent large-nucleus signal with frac_large_nucleus z +24 to +32 and cell/nuclear area z +17 to +32 in all six wells from 0.01 to 30 uM, plus microscopist suggestion of Aurora inhibitors and 6/10 Aurora neighbors on reference-atlas comparison. Preserved tubulin signal and a flat mitotic-like feature helped exclude microtubule poisons and Eg5 arrest, which fit Aurora B inhibition-induced hyper-polyploidy described in PMID 39779678 and cytokinesis-failure polyploidy in PMID 20484572.

What I glossed over was the dose-response shape: frac_large_nucleus rho -0.77 and nuc_dna_integrated rho -0.89 were negative, not a clean saturation increase, suggesting high-dose cell loss, segmentation merging, or toxicity on top of polyploidy. I described integrated DNA as increased while the correlation was decreasing with dose, and I over-read constant frac_mitotic_like as proof of no mitotic effect without a phospho-H3 or time-course.

Acquisition reinforced the blind spot by sampling only the saturated regime; the lowest 0.01 uM well was already maximal so EC50 and onset were never defined. Next time I would extend below 0.01 uM and add a direct Aurora-activity readout rather than relying on size plus atlas match alone.

What was right:
- Giant-nucleus plus enlarged cell_area and nuc_area z-scores >+17 across all doses correctly flagged potent polyploidy from failed cytokinesis rather than DNA-damage enlargement
- Microscopist call combined with 6/10 Aurora atlas neighbors correctly outweighed 2/10 DNA-damage and 2/10 DNA-replication neighbors
- Preserved tub_mean and flat frac_mitotic_like across wells correctly argued against microtubule stabilizers/destabilizers and Eg5 mitotic arrest

What was wrong or missed:
- Misread dose_response e13 nuc_dna_integrated rho -0.89 p=0.019 as supporting increased DNA content when slope was negative, missing possible high-dose loss or segmentation effect
- Treated dose_response e11 frac_large_nucleus rho -0.77 as early saturation without testing lower doses below 0.01 uM to define onset/EC50, leaving acquisition choice saturated
- Over-interpreted constant frac_mitotic_like in e12 as absence of mitotic involvement without phospho-H3 Ser10 or time-lapse to detect transient Aurora mitotic delay

Proposed next experiment: Low-dose titration below 0.01 uM with phospho-Histone H3 Ser10 immunofluorescence, DNA-content flow cytometry, and live imaging to confirm loss of Aurora activity and capture binucleation/failed cytokinesis onset and polyploid DNA peaks.
